title: Artificial Minds, Cultural Shadows: Cultural Alignment, Identity, and Voice Across Multiple Large Language Models
Artificial intelligence companionship for loneliness in older adults: An interview with Vijeth Iyengar and Elizabeth Broadbent
abstract_raw:
"MIT Science Policy Review spoke with Dr. Elizabeth Broadbent and Dr. Vijeth Iyengar, two leading experts in human-robot interaction and global aging, about loneliness in later life and the role that artificial intelligence companions have been proposed to play in addressing it. Loneliness carries consequences for both mental and physical health. As older adult populations grow rapidly while younger ones shrink, social isolation has become an increasingly common feature of global aging. Artificial intelligence (AI) companions, from pet-like therapeutic robots to large language model chatbots, have emerged as one proposed response. Such technologies have raised new questions about the ethics of elder care and the role of AI in human connection.

Dr. Broadbent is a Professor of Health Psychology at the University of Auckland, with a background in electrical engineering, whose research focuses on human-robot interaction, AI companions, and how robots can support human health. Dr. Iyengar is a cognitive neuroscientist and the Senior Director of Global Aging at AARP, with prior policy experience across three U.S. administrations on aging and brain health."

title: From data literacy to AI-integrated Laboratory 4.0
Regulating towards independence: EU AI policy and ethics
abstract_raw:
MIT Science Policy Review spoke with Gianluca Sgueo about the evolving landscape of digital public policy and AI regulation in Europe. Sgueo is a Senior Associate Researcher at the Center for Digitalization, Democracy and Innovation of the Brussels School of Governance. He authored The Design of Digital Democracy, in which he examines how design principles of mass technology, such as simplicity, speed, and singularity, reshape democratic spaces in ways that often undermine meaningful civic engagement. Sgueo was a policy advisor at the Digital Transformation Team of the Italian Government and Head of Communication and Stakeholder Engagement of the Office of the Italian Prime Minister. He studies e-government, the gamification of public services, and the tension between digital innovation and democratic inclusion. 

In our conversation, Sgueo reflects on the EU AI Act's risk-based regulatory approach, the structural barriers to European digital sovereignty, and the influence of major US technology companies on EU governance frameworks. He highlights the gap between AI ethics principles and their translation into binding legislation, drawing on the trajectory of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) (hyperlink{leg_1}{4}) as a precedent for durable regulatory impact. Sgueo also addresses the democratic risks of agentic AI, the under representation of cultures and languages other than English in large language models, and the urgent need for technological literacy as a foundation for inclusive digital democracy. He concludes with a cautionary note on emerging ideological currents that seek to decouple technological development from democratic accountability.

title: Artificial intelligence-supported segmentation of cardiac anatomy in open-heart surgery videos
abstract_raw: Accurate identification of anatomical structures is essential for safe congenital cardiac surgery and for the development of assistive robotic systems. However, scalable annotation of open-heart surgical video remains a major challenge due to dynamic tissue motion, occlusion, and anatomical variability. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a human-in-the-loop segmentation and tracking pipeline for congenital open-heart surgery videos. A dataset of 72 annotated video clips comprising 27,461 frames was created from routine recordings of congenital cardiac surgery. Independent tracking evaluation was performed on 6 video clips (2,400 frames) from three surgical cases that were not used for training or validation. A hybrid framework combining fine-tuned Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2) for propagation-based tracking and YOLOv11 for detection-based monitoring was implemented and evaluated. Fine-tuning improved temporal tracking performance compared with the pretrained model, increasing the mean IoU from 82.1% to 92.2% and the proportion of frames with IoU ≥ 90% from 48.2% to 72.3% on the independent evaluation dataset. A graphical user interface enabled efficient dataset creation, reducing annotation time by approximately 40-fold compared with manual tracing. This study demonstrates that domain-adapted foundation-model tracking can provide robust anatomical tracking in a dynamic open surgical environment and offers a scalable framework for future assistive and robotic cardiac applications.

title: Enhancing EFL learners’ speaking performance through ChatGPT-assisted practice: evidence from complexity, accuracy, and fluency measures
keywords: Asian-Pacific Journal of Second and Foreign Language Education
abstract_raw: This study examined whether ChatGPT-assisted speaking practice could strengthen English as a Foreign Language speaking development in an IELTS preparation context. Sixty-five intermediate Iranian learners participated in a ten-week quasi-experimental intervention, with one group receiving structured ChatGPT-supported speaking practice and a comparison group receiving teacher-led instruction. Learner performance was assessed through IELTS-aligned speaking tasks and analyzed using complexity, accuracy, and fluency indicators. The findings showed a clear pedagogical advantage of ChatGPT-assisted practice for syntactic complexity and fluency, while accuracy improved over time in both groups without a distinct between-group advantage. These results suggested that large language model-based interaction could create conditions that encouraged longer turns, richer language production, and faster speech delivery, particularly when learners received sustained opportunities for low-pressure, adaptive oral practice beyond limited classroom speaking time. At the same time, the pattern for accuracy indicated that generative AI should be integrated as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, teacher guidance, especially for form-focused feedback. The study contributed evidence from an underrepresented EFL context and supported a blended instructional model in which ChatGPT expanded speaking opportunities, promoted learner autonomy, and enhanced key dimensions of oral performance within communicative language teaching.
